what_matters.head: DBS, UOB and OCBC fell another 4â€“5% by 12:05 SGT, a second day down, after JPMorgan warned that high long-term bond yields will hurt Southeast Asian banks' third-quarter earnings.
what_matters.detail: JPMorgan's analyst Harsh Wardhan Modi told clients in a 7 Oct note to trim their holdings, writing that the surprise in third-quarter results 'is likely skewed negative'. Bloomberg: the three banks were the biggest drag on the Straits Times Index, the worst performer in Asia this morning. On Wednesday OCBC had already fallen 5.9% after Citi cut it to sell; DBS fell 1.4% and UOB 2.9% that day.

what_matters.head: Samsung's preliminary third-quarter operating profit came in at 107.4 trillion won, just above the analysts' average of 106.1 trillion (LSEG).
what_matters.detail: That is almost nine times a year earlier and Samsung's first quarter above 100 trillion won; revenue was about 195 trillion won. The preliminary release gives only those two figures, with no division or HBM detail; full results come later in October.

what_matters.head: Micron's Taoyuan union won its strike vote: 1,994 of its 2,258 members voted yes (88%), where it needed more than half of all members.
what_matters.detail: The vote gives a right to strike, not a date. No date is set; the union says a surprise strike is one option and has called members to a protest in Taipei on 19 Oct. Micron's board meets 8â€“9 Oct in the US, and the union expects an answer on profit-sharing; Micron says it will keep talking through dialogue and mediation. The unions say the Taoyuan and Taichung plants make more than 60% of Micron's output.
